incidents.cause: The pilot's improper flare while landing. Contributing to the accident was the gusty wind condition.
An inflight bird strike, which resulted in wing spar damage.
A loss of engine power due to contamination of the helicopter's fuel supply.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for the gusting wind, which resulted in an excessive descent rate and hard landing.
Separation of the auxiliary fuel tank cap, which entered the tail rotor system. Contributing to the accident was the lack of a fuel tank cap restraint.
The pilot's failure to remove the right skid trailer tie-down before attempting to take off, which resulted in a dynamic roll-over.
The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a quartering tailwind.
An inadvertent collision with a deer during takeoff and the airplane’s subsequent departure from the runway and impact with a tree.
An in-flight fire and subsequent total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined due to extensive impact and fire damage, followed by a loss of airplane control.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain control of the airplane during a go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
The pilot’s failure to maintain airspeed and angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of aircraft control in gusty and turbulent wind conditions.
an inadvertent fall by the passenger while exiting the lavatory when the seat belt light was illuminated.
The pilot’s failure to maintain a proper descent rate, which resulted in a hard landing.
A loss of brake fluid for reasons that could not be determined, which resulted in a loss of braking effectiveness during landing.
